title: Purge pilot identifiers from application logic and add a CI grep that keeps them out
description:
The pilot beat is hard-coded in about 40 places. Python: 'AI-ML-research' appears as a default in 28 call sites (src/papyrus_newsroom/tactus_runtime.py:320-472, newsroom.py:1251-2463, papyrus_newsroom/cli.py:405,459 argparse defaults, papyrus_content/assignments_workflow.py:125-602, edition_planning.py:45, tavily_deep_research.py:527, email_submissions.py:31, reference_discovery.py:32, newsroom_commands.py:795, papyrus_content/cli.py:921 'AI-ML-journalism'); src/papyrus/operator/config.py:48 falls back to 'threat-intelligence'; coverage_theme.py:21-44 hard-codes DEFAULT_SECTIONS ['culture','methods','business','law'], SECTION_ALIASES and SECTION_RESEARCH_LENSES (the AI-in-video-games demo lenses) for every publication; model names gpt-5.4-mini and gpt-5.4-nano appear about 40 times in Python and in every .tac header while model_defaults.py has three constants. TypeScript: lib/site-brand.ts:172,176 reference brand carries corpusKey 'threat-intelligence' and publicationName 'Anthus Threat Intelligence'; app/page.tsx:129,178 placeholder copy and alt text name the TI emblem; lib/themed-image.ts:26 special-cases /seed-art/threat-intelligence/. Backend: amplify/site-backend.ts:153,158,159,508 default corpus 'AI-ML-research', domain p.apyr.us and a hosted zone id; email-submission-processor/handler.py:33; console-chat-responder/resource.ts:113 hard-codes SSM ARNs for one Amplify app id.

Fix: one default_corpus_key() in Python that reads corpora/papyrus-steering.yml canonicalTopicSet.corpusKey and raises when absent; load section lenses and aliases from NewsroomSection rows (or a sections YAML) and fail on unknown sections; one per-role model map in model_defaults.py referenced by Python and passed to .tac agents as input; make corpusKey and publicationName required brand fields; make the backend domain, zone, corpus and SSM path required PapyrusSite.backend config that fails synth when missing. Add a CI check (a small Python script under procedures/ run from tests.yml) that fails when 'AI-ML-research', 'threat-intelligence', 'p.apyr.us', '/Users/' or 'gpt-5' appears outside corpora/, publications/, config, docs and tests.

Done when: the CI grep passes with an allowlist limited to config and publication folders.

Source: full code review of develop @ e9b1923 on 2026-10-17 (https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f01a3c9f-7fad-4df2-8a15-ac6c27cc83ed). Branch from origin/develop, name the branch after this issue, open a PR into develop, and record branch, PR link and verification in a comment here before closing.

comments.text:
Handoff for the DevOps session (PPY-8a7e7a): parts 1 and 2 (PRs 227, 229) make these Python and .tac inputs required with no pilot fallback, so the deployed pipeline must supply them. Nothing in amplify/ was changed by the cleanup, so the current defaults still apply until DevOps decides to make them required in synth.

Already supplied by site-backend.ts to the inbound processor Lambda: PAPYRUS_INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN (from the env default p.apyr.us). Must start being supplied explicitly: PAPYRUS_PUBLIC_SITE_BASE_URL is hard-coded to https://p.apyr.us at amplify/site-backend.ts:513 (works, but is a pilot literal), and PAPYRUS_INBOUND_EMAIL_CORPUS_KEY (default AI-ML-research at site-backend.ts:163, ses-inbound-receive/handler.ts:327).

Remaining pilot defaults in amplify/ that should become required PapyrusSite.backend config (fail synth when missing): inbound email domain (site-backend.ts:158, ses-inbound-receive/handler.ts:32), inbound corpus key (site-backend.ts:163, handler.ts:327, assignment-action/handler.ts:885), Route 53 hosted zone id and name (site-backend.ts:164-165), public site base URL (site-backend.ts:513), and the per-app SSM parameter ARNs for Amplify app dbsyytcm9drqa in console-chat-responder/resource.ts:113-114. Also lib/site-brand.ts:172,176 reference brand corpusKey and publicationName. Python callers now read PAPYRUS_INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN and PAPYRUS_PUBLIC_SITE_BASE_URL (or publicSite.baseUrl in the Papyrus config) and raise if absent.
